stories.headline: Russia launches major attack on Ukraine’s energy grid, killing seven and causing emergency power cuts

sources.body: Russia launched its heaviest combined assault on Ukraine’s energy infrastructure in months on Wednesday, killing seven people and triggering emergency power cuts in Kyiv and nearby regions. The strikes came as officials warned of a difficult winter amid Russian attacks on Ukraine’s power and heating infrastructure.
sources.headline: Russia launches major attack on Ukraine’s energy grid, causing power cuts

sources.body:
When Vladimir Putin arrived to address Russia's parliament on Wednesday, a warm welcome was guaranteed.

"The Special Election Operation", as one Russian newspaper dubbed last month's legislative vote , has produced a State Duma even more pro-Putin than anything before it.

The ruling party, United Russia, now has more MPs than ever.

It allows the Kremlin to claim it has been handed a huge mandate from the Russian people.

Are there any signs he is prepared to halt what he calls the special military operation? Or should we brace for further escalation in Ukraine and in tensions with Europe?

On Thursday I'll be watching to see whether Russia's leader sheds light on his plans during an appearance at the Valdai Discussion Club in Moscow. Traditionally the president's speech at this annual foreign policy forum provides insight into Putin's world view.

Right now, everything points to Putin continuing Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine: despite his country's huge battlefield losses to date and the damage being done to Russia's economy.

Putin's speeches and statements suggest he remains confident that Russia can secure a military victory.

Judging by what is being reported in Russian media, Moscow is encouraged by the shortage of air defence missiles in Ukraine, as well as the expectation that Russian strikes this winter will increase pressure on Ukrainians. Kyiv has spoken of its difficulty in shooting down Russia's ballistic missiles and new jet-powered drones, which have been targeting Ukraine every day.

The Kremlin has made no secret of the fact it wants European states to slash their military and financial backing for Ukraine: the kind of support Moscow says is prolonging the war - or, rather, getting in the way of a Russian victory.

To achieve this, Western officials believe Russia has been sending not so subtle signals.

They accuse Moscow of waging an escalating hybrid war on European countries through cyber-attacks, acts of sabotage, and Russian drones violating European airspace. In Germany, a drone carrying an explosive device was found close to Ukrainian cargo planes at Leipzig airport.

A covert campaign in the "grey zone", that space between peace and war.

This week I asked Russia's foreign minister, Sergei Lavrov, does he admit that his country is waging a hybrid war against European countries?

"Do you mean when we destroy drones and missiles that Britain and continental Europe are supplying Ukraine with, and which are used to attack us?" Lavrov replied.

"If you admit your weapons are being used to strike us and we destroy them, call it whatever you want. But I have no doubt this is a war Europe is waging against us. We've been saying so for a long time."

That, indeed, has been the official Russian stance for some time: that what is happening in Ukraine amounts to a European war on Russia. It is a narrative that skips over the fact that in 2022 it was the Kremlin that launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine, and that Russia continues to wage war there.

How far would Russia go to sever European support for Kyiv?
sources.headline: Rosenberg: Putin shows no sign of stopping the war as Russia doubles down on Ukraine

stories.headline: Pakistan launches deadly air raids in Afghanistan

sources.body:
Kabul says the strikes killed 9 women and children in Kunar and Helmand provinces, as Pakistan says 22 fighters killed.

Pakistan has targeted “camps and hideouts” used by armed groups in two locations in Afghanistan and killed at least 22 fighters, its Ministry of Information says.

The ministry gave the details of air attacks by Pakistani forces on Thursday, even as Kabul accused Islamabad of killing at least nine women and children in attacks on its Kunar and Helmand provinces.

Al Jazeera could not independently verify the claims made by both sides.

Zabihullah Mujahid, the chief spokesman for Afghanistan’s Taliban government, said the attacks took place late on Wednesday and that at least nine people were killed and 11 others wounded.

In a post on X, he said the attacks on northeastern Kunar and southern Helmand provinces destroyed three houses.

“We condemn this act and consider it an aggression and crime against all accepted principles,” Mujahid wrote.

Pakistan’s Information Ministry said the attacks were based on “credible intelligence” and targeted two armed groups – the Pakistan Taliban, also known by the acronym TTP, and the Balochistan Liberation Army (BLA).

“Targets were destroyed with precision and initial reports suggest killing of twenty two terrorists,” the ministry said in a statement on X.

“Large quantities of weapons ⁠and ammunition stored at these hideouts was also destroyed,” it ⁠said.

The attacks come amid an escalation in fighting between the neighbouring countries after three months of relative calm. Islamabad accuses Kabul of harbouring armed groups, including the TTP, and carrying out cross-border attacks on its territory.

Reporting from Islamabad, Al Jazeera’s Kamal Hyder said the BLA has been responsible for an increasing number of attacks in Pakistan’s restive Balochistan province, while the Pakistan Taliban has been carrying out attacks in the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province.

In November 2022, a brief ceasefire between the TTP and the Pakistani government, with the Taliban in Afghanistan mediating, broke down, following which armed groups have been staging an increasing number of attacks, Hyder said.

“Every time there is an attack on the Pakistani side, Pakistan then carries out air strikes,” he said.

The Afghan government ‌denies harbouring armed groups and says the Pakistani attacks have targeted civilian homes, killing and wounding women and children.

The United Nations Assistance Mission in Afghanistan said last week it had documented more than 1,100 civilian casualties in the country in cross-border violence so far this year.
sources.headline: Pakistan launches deadly air attacks on Afghanistan

stories.headline: Investigation opens after Flydubai co-pilot allegedly attacks captain on Israel-bound flight

sources.body: The United Arab Emirates on Thursday launched an investigation into the Israel-bound FlyDubai FZ1073 flight from Dubai in which a copilot allegedly stabbed his captain in an apparent attempt to crash the plane. The UAE’s chief prosecutor said the possibility of a terror link will be probed. Follow our liveblog for all the latest developments.
sources.headline: Live: UAE probes possible 'terror' link in attack on FlyDubai flight to Israel

sources.body:
Benjamin Netanyahu says too early to tell who may have been behind plane incident as carrier halts all flights to Israel

The motive, background and affiliation of the Omani co-pilot who stabbed his captain in an apparent attempt to crash an Israel-bound flight from Dubai remains unknown, as international teams open investigations into the incident.

Israeli passengers intervened to stop the attack on Wednesday, restraining the co-pilot, while a reserve crew in the plane was able to stabilise the plummeting plane and ultimately land it safely in Saudi Arabia.

The plane had more than 170 people onboard and Israeli officials praised the bravery of those who intervened, announcing that four of the Israeli passengers would receive a “heroism” award for preventing a potential disaster.

Saudi investigators, who initially detained the co-pilot upon landing, were cooperating with the United Arab Emirates , the US, Oman and Israel to try to determine the attacker’s motive, a regional official familiar with the investigation said. “All possible scenarios, from terrorism to mental disorders, are being looked into. Nothing is ruled out for now,” they told the Associated Press.

Benjamin Netanyahu said that it was still not known who may have been ultimately behind the apparent attempted attack. The Israeli prime minister told Fox News it was “too early to say” if there was any Iranian involvement.

“We’ll get to the root of this attacker, whether he had accomplices, whether Iran was behind it. I think we’ll find out very soon,” Netanyahu said.

It came just days after Netanyahu warned of an unspecified security threat to Israel that could come during its October election. The Israeli military had said before the incident it had no specific intelligence of an imminent threat, while the opposition leader Yair Lapid said that a security briefing on Tuesday night included no mention of a related threat.

Other Israeli officials, including the defence minister, Israel Katz, and the ambassador to the UN, Danny Danon, suggested the incident was a “terror attack”, with the Israeli foreign ministry briefing its diplomats that the attack was against Israel and its relationship with the UAE.

Danon told Fox News that Israel had “no doubt it was a terror attack from a radical individual”, but said that until now investigators had not established any link to a specific organisation or state.

Donald Trump suggested the co-pilot was “perhaps a terrorist or perhaps a whack job”, while telling reporters at the White House that he and Netanyahu had spoken at length.

Netanyahu also spoke to the president of the UAE, Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, who agreed to Israel’s involvement in the investigation.

Flydubai said its flights to and from Israel would be suspended while the investigation took place and urged all parties “to refrain from premature speculation while authorities gather the facts”.

The UAE announced on Thursday that it would be conducting its own investigation of the incident, which started about two and a half hours after takeoff from Dubai. It said its investigators had begun to look into the attacker’s motive and if he had any links to any “terrorist purpose”.
sources.headline: Motive behind flydubai cockpit stabbing unknown as international investigation opens

sources.body:
Israel’s prime minister said one of the pilots stabbed the other and then tried to crash the plane.

A flight from the United Arab Emirates to Israel was diverted to Saudi Arabia after one of the plane’s two pilots attempted to stab the other in the cockpit on Wednesday.

UAE’s Attorney General Hamad Saif al-Shamsi ordered an investigation into the incident on Thursday. According to his office, the investigation team would “collect information and evidence to determine the truth of the incident, its circumstances, details, and motives, and to verify the extent of its connection to any terrorist activity or purpose, or the existence of prior planning or direction for it”.

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, meanwhile, said it was too early to declare a motive for the incident, which occurred on a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv, while responding to a question on whether he thought Iran was behind the incident.

Netanyahu added that Israel would “possibly” be participating in the probe into the incident.

“It’s too early to say; the attacking pilot is … now being investigated in Saudi Arabia. I think he’ll be taken to the Emirates, where he comes from, or at least where he left, where he flew off from, and we’ll be following and possibly also participating in this investigation,” Netanyahu said in an interview with Fox News host Sean Hannity on the Hannity programme.

The Flydubai flight FZ1073 was diverted as it flew from Dubai to Tel Aviv through Jordanian airspace, prompting Israel to deploy warplanes, the Reuters news agency reported. Passengers on the flight reached Israel safely on Wednesday after the copilot’s attempt to crash the aircraft was foiled, Israeli officials said.

The struggle began when he stabbed the pilot and sent the jet plunging nearly 14,000 feet (4,267 metres) in less than 30 seconds.

Earlier, Netanyahu had noted that one of the pilots had stabbed the other and then tried to crash the plane. He added that Israel was preparing for other “potential threats” after the incident.

“At this early stage, the underlying reasons and motives behind this event are unknown and remain subject to a formal investigation,” a Flydubai spokesperson said in a statement. “We urge all parties to refrain from premature speculation while authorities gather the facts.”

At Saudi Arabia’s Tabuk airport, where the plane landed, officials said the plane’s captain and first officer were taken to hospital after sustaining injuries, according to a statement from Tabuk airport, carried by Saudi state-run Al Ekhbariya TV.

India’s embassy in Saudi Arabia later identified the injured captain as Indian national Smit Machchhar. It said he was receiving treatment at a hospital in Tabuk and was reported to be in stable condition, adding that it was in contact with his family and Saudi authorities.

The UAE has become a popular holiday destination for Israeli tourists since the countries normalised ties in 2020 . Here’s what we know about what happened.

Footage taken on board the plane appears to show the injured pilot lying on the cabin floor with several stab wounds, and a passenger with a bloody head wound.
sources.headline: What happened on the diverted Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv?

stories.headline: Tennessee death-row prisoner Christa Pike survives a failed execution after two lethal injections

sources.body:
Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike has been taken to hospital after an attempt to execute her by two lethal injections failed, her lawyer says.

Her legal team filed an emergency motion to halt the convicted murderer's execution as it was happening, saying: "Ms Pike has lost consciousness and still has a heartbeat and is audibly snoring."

One of her attorneys told the BBC that Pike, 50, was now "being provided life-saving measures" in hospital after two syringes of pentobarbital had been administered.

Pike was sentenced to death in 1996 for the murder of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer. Her execution was the subject of a last-minute legal battle.

This culminated in the US Supreme Court allowing the lethal injections to go ahead.

Pike was 18 when she and her then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Slemmer, whom they had met at a job training camp for troubled teens.

Slemmer's mother May Martinez was among those who wanted the execution to take place. Speaking to NBC News after Wednesday evening's events, she said: "It was a mess."

The attempted execution took place at Riverbend Maximum Security Institution in Nashville at about 20:00 local time (01:00 GMT on Thursday).

Pike was given two doses of the chemical pentobarbital, and the curtain in the witness room was closed twice, the AP news agency reported.

Media were at some point asked to leave, the news agency said.

AP added that Tennessee's execution protocol calls for a secondary set of drug syringes in case the person being put to death does not die after the first set. But it does not spell out what happens if the subject is alive after the second set.

In a statement reported by US media, Tennessee Governor Bill Lee said he had ordered "a comprehensive, third-party review to determine exactly what occurred". He said the year's last remaining execution would not go ahead as planned.

The attempted execution of Pike was not the first in the state in 2026 that did not unfold as planned. The execution of Tony Carruthers, who was convicted of kidnapping and murdering three people in 1994, was postponed in May after staff were unable to find a vein to administer a lethal drug.

The Tennessee Department of Correction has said it stands by all the actions it took during the attempted execution of Pike.

"The Tennessee Department of Correction followed every step of the State's lawful, established execution protocol approved by the Attorney General's Office," department spokesperson Dorinda Carter told the Tennessean newspaper.

"The lethal injection chemical in the protocol has consistently been effective, and the protocol does not allow for additional procedures beyond what was carried out this evening. Christa Pike has been transported to an off-site medical facility," she said.

Pike's legal team said in a statement to the Tennessean newspaper: "Tonight the State of Tennessee once again failed to carry out a lawful execution.

"We take no pleasure in being right, but the concerns raised by Ms Pike proved to be true: difficult vein access, blown veins, degraded pentobarbital, no emergency medical care available when things inevitably go wrong, all under a protocol that remains veiled in secrecy."
sources.headline: US death row inmate survives execution attempt after two lethal injections

sources.body: Christa Pike, who has been on death row for more than 30 years for torturing and murdering a classmate, was on Wednesday set to be executed, but the lethal injections meant to kill her failed. Pike was then transported to a medical facility, but except for the fact that she is still alive, her lawyers said they had not been informed about her condition.
sources.headline: Execution of convicted US killer Christa Pike fails despite two lethal injections

sources.body:
The only woman on Tennessee ‘death row’ is in hospital after two injections failed to kill her.

Two doses of a lethal injection drug have failed to kill Christa Gail Pike , a 50-year-old woman who was due to be executed on Wednesday. Pike was taken to hospital after it was found that her heart was still beating following the procedure.

Pike would have been the first woman in more than 200 years to be put to death in Tennessee and was the only woman on the state’s death row. Her attempted execution with doses of the sedative pentobarbital went ahead despite a last-minute stay by a federal appeals court on Wednesday, which was overturned just an hour before her execution by the Supreme Court.

Human rights experts said the botched execution illustrates why the death penalty is inhumane and should be abolished.

Clive Stafford Smith, a human rights lawyer who has represented many American death row inmates as well as detainees held at the notorious Guantanamo Bay detention centre, told Al Jazeera: “I’ve been in the execution chamber with six of my clients and it’s never the clinical process they’d have you believe. And it’s always a desperate midnight struggle to stop it.”

He added: “In the end, you have to question whether this makes the world a better, more civilised place. Why, indeed, do we kill people to prove that killing people is wrong?”

Ahead of the planned execution, Morris Tidball-Binz, the UN special rapporteur on arbitrary executions, told the UK’s Times newspaper: “If executed, Christa Pike would be a victim of torture to death. This will be a gross violation of human rights.”

Here’s what we know about what happens when an execution goes wrong.

Pike was found guilty of the murder of another young woman she had viewed as a romantic rival, when she was aged 18, more than 30 years ago.

In January 1995, Pike, her 17-year-old boyfriend Tadaryl Shipp and 18-year-old Shadolla Peterson lured Colleen Slemmer, 19, into a wooded area and tortured and killed her. All four were students at a Job Corps vocational centre in Knoxville.

The case attracted huge public interest, especially after it was revealed that the attackers had carved a pentagram into Slemmer’s chest, which Shipp later admitted to doing. Pike, who delivered the killing blow to the victim’s head, smashing her skull, kept a piece of Slemmer’s skull afterwards.

Pike and Shipp confessed and were convicted of first-degree murder in 1996. Pike was sentenced to death; Shipp, who was 17 at the time and therefore ineligible for the death penalty, received life with the possibility of parole.

Her case is highly unusual in that she is a woman and was a teenager when she carried out the murder. Other death row inmates who were convicted at the age of 18 – all men – have had their sentences commuted to life in prison without parole.

“Christa is a 50-year-old remorseful woman who understands her actions,” her lawyers wrote. They also argued that Pike had been the victim of appalling childhood abuse – including two rapes when she was aged 11 and 17.
sources.headline: Christa Pike execution fails: What next when a lethal injection is botched?

stories.headline: Swiss glaciers lose 20% of their ice in five years, threatening water supplies

sources.body:
Swiss glaciers have suffered a near-record loss of ice in 2026, new data shows, as intense summer heatwaves take their toll on Alpine peaks.

More than 5% of the country's remaining glacier ice has disappeared in the last 12 months, which scientists say is "extraordinary".

They warn that such rapid melting is no longer a surprise given the pace of climate change, but it could threaten water supplies for farming, hydropower and transport in the decades ahead.

The loss of glacier ice can also destabilise mountain slopes and increase the risk of landslides in some places - which can lead to flash flooding in extreme cases, as seen in Nepal in August.

There were multiple factors involved in that event, which was triggered when a large area of bedrock and glacier ice collapsed.

But scientists say long-term glacier thinning and the thawing of frozen ground likely raised the risks.

The notable finding from this latest report is not so much that Swiss glaciers are shrinking - which is to be expected in our warming climate, driven primarily by fossil fuel emissions - but the sheer pace of melting.

Until recently, glaciologists in the Alps considered 2% of ice lost in a single year to be "extreme". This year has seen an estimated 5.5% disappear.

"It's really just disastrous," said Dr Matthias Huss, director of Glacier Monitoring Switzerland, which produced the report.

Swiss glaciers started the summer in an already difficult place, covered by less snow than usual after a mild winter.

And much of that snow disappeared quickly in the early and intense heatwaves of May and June , exposing the glacier ice below.

Bare ice is darker and less reflective than fresh snow, so absorbs more of the Sun's energy.

That left glaciers vulnerable to melting even faster in subsequent heatwaves.

"Ten years ago, I wouldn't have thought that it's possible to lose glaciers so quickly," said Dr Fabien Maussion, a glaciologist at the University of Bristol, who was not involved in the Swiss report.

"What's happened over the summer now is extremely distressing… but at the same time it was to be expected from a climate scientist's perspective," he added.

Meltwater from glaciers can be an important source of water for irrigation, hydropower and even shipping traffic during hot, dry conditions.

Scientists estimate that Swiss glaciers released 2.2 trillion litres of meltwater between July and September.

Although that helped to ease water shortages this summer, it has rapidly diminished the frozen supply.

The loss of ice could pose long-term challenges, Huss warned, with smaller glaciers unable to top up water levels to the same extent.

"Every drop of water that runs off during these heatwaves is kind of old water that's been stocked in the glacier ice centuries or decades ago," said Huss.

"It's helping us [now] but it's unsustainable, so we won't have it at [our] disposal in the next heatwave."

The River Rhine reached record lows in places this summer , affecting shipping navigation routes and increasing transport costs.
sources.headline: Swiss glaciers suffer 'disastrous' year of ice loss, threatening water supplies

sources.body:
Alpine regions in Europe experiencing extreme glacier collapse due to heat-trapping effects of fossil fuel pollution

Switzerland has lost almost one-fifth of its ice in just five years, research has found, in a dramatic reshaping of the Alpine country whose big white glaciers have been reduced to moonlike rock deserts, scientists say.

Swiss glaciers shrank by 5.5% in the first eight months of 2026, according to an annual monitoring report, after a summer of scorching heatwaves that followed a winter with little snow. The reduction in ice volume falls just shy of the record set in 2022 and brings the total loss of glacier ice since 2021 to 19.4%.

Matthias Huss, a glaciologist at ETH Zürich and lead author of the report , said many people do not realise how fast glaciers are retreating, or that just one generation ago some now-barren sites used to sit beneath hundreds of metres of ice. The scientists have not yet compiled a formal tally of lost glaciers this year but said they had witnessed the death of a number of small ones.

“I visited one last week and it’s so impressive to stand in this moonlike landscape where there was a big layer of ice – an extensive glacier – just a few years ago,” said Huss. “And now it’s a rock desert where there’s some scattered blocks of old ice still lying around and melting on the hot rocks.”

The report, a collaboration between the Swiss Glacier Monitoring Network and the Swiss Commission for Cryosphere Observation, found the mean thickness of individual glaciers fell by between 2.5 metres and 4 metres in 2026. Huss said scientists were increasingly seeing glaciers collapse from the inside – the result of internal streams beneath the ice that excavate caverns – rather than simply retreating from surface heat.

“You have huge holes like cheese in the middle of the ice that have collapsing roofs,” said Huss. “These are processes that tear the glaciers apart and make them retreat even faster.”

Europe is warming twice as fast as the global average from the heat-trapping effects of fossil fuel pollution and the destruction of nature, with Alpine regions experiencing some of the most dramatic changes.

Analysis published by MeteoSwiss on Tuesday found the summer half-year from April to September was the hottest and driest it had been since records began in 1864. In that time, humanity has filled the atmosphere with 1.8tn tons of carbon dioxide and heated the planet by about 1.4C.

The heat this summer was worse than in 2022 but Swiss ice loss just missed the record-breaking levels set that year. The scientists attributed this to limited deposits of Saharan dust, which foul the snow and prevent it from reflecting sunlight, as well as slightly greater snow cover at the end of winter and more sunlight in the summer.

The most pressing stories and debates for Europeans – from identity to economics to the environment

Huss visited the former Plattalvafirn , or Griess glacier, in September, which used to cover a mountain flank but lost 99% of its area in just 20 years. The glacier was the subject of some of the most detailed monitoring in the world in the 1950s and Huss worked with its data when he was a PhD student.
sources.headline: ‘Explosion of melt rates’: 20% of Swiss glaciers lost in five years

stories.headline: Trump administration cuts Pentagon generals and admirals by 20%

sources.body: US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth said Wednesday that his department had cut 20 percent of US admirals, generals and officers who did not fit his vision. "Simple translation of that: no fatties, no trannies, no beardos, no weirdos, no wimps, no radicals. Just warriors – just tough, ready, committed troops," he said.
sources.headline: Pentagon’s Hegseth says 20 percent of US generals, admirals cut, ‘no fatties, no trannies’

sources.body:
US Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth has confirmed the firing of 20% of top military leadership, while stressing a "warrior ethos", and plans for a new base and autonomous warfare command.

In a fiery speech to top brass at Marine Corps Base Quantico in Virginia, he shared a variety of new initiatives, as well as adding to a round of personnel cuts in 2025.

There are over 800 active-duty generals and admirals across the Army, Navy, Marine Corps, Air Force and Space Force, according to the latest department tally.

When Hegseth assembled military leaders at Quantico in September 2025, he criticised the department as too "woke" and slammed leaders, saying "fat generals and admirals" is "a bad look".

In his remarks on Wednesday, Hegseth referred to last year's Quantico speech as Liberation Day, saying that those who were not on board with his changes, "well, they no longer work here".

"We are no longer the woke department or the weak department," Hegseth said.

The defence secretary singled out groups he said he did not want in the military, including transgender people, overweight people and people with beards.

"The ideological clowns are out. The patriotic cowboys are in with testosterone testing on top. Diversity is not our strength. Unity is our strength," he said.

Hegseth also announced the creation of the Autonomous Warfare Command, aimed at easing the procurement of robotics and drones for warfare, "supercharged" with artificial intelligence.

A new Office of Religious Affairs, cadets programme partnering with US universities, and what Hegseth called "the next great American [military] base" were also announced.

The new office will "protect budgets, demand infrastructure, and strengthen religious support", he said.

Hegseth did not mention the location or funding source for the new base, but called on US states to "bring us your best sales pitch".

Hegseth's firings are the latest in a broader overhaul of the US military under his leadership, seeking to insert what he calls a "war fighter ethos" into the defence department, including a rebrand of his office as the Department of War.

According to the BBC's US partner CBS News, at least 20 generals, admirals and civilian military leaders have been terminated or quit their jobs since Hegseth became defence secretary.

This includes the firing of the chairman of the joint chiefs of staff and top uniformed officials in the Army, Navy and Air Force.

"Now the media calls that a purge," Hegseth said on Wednesday. "I call it accountability, and long overdue. And frankly, the bare minimum."

Federal law sets a limit to the number of general and flag officers. There is no requirement that unfilled positions be replaced.

Amid the shakeup, Hegseth also has been accused by various civil rights groups, including the NAACP and the National Women's Law Center, of blocking the military promotions of black people and women.

George Washington University political science professor Alexander Downes highlighted these concerns to the BBC, describing Hegseth's track record as "a little suspect".
sources.headline: 'Clowns out, cowboys in,' says Hegseth as a fifth of generals and admirals are fired

stories.headline: Republicans weigh Trump’s turnout power against the risk he poses in competitive midterm races

sources.body: Republicans know President Donald Trump's unpopularity poses a big problem for them in November. They also recognize he may be their only option to avoid a wipeout. Five weeks before Election Day, many Republicans are facing a damned-if-they-do, damned-if-they-don’t dilemma. Some candidates in close races are wary of alienating undecided voters by campaigning alongside Trump and the baggage that comes with him: High gas prices, voters’ persistent economic concerns and the prolonged war in Iran. But keeping the president at arm’s length could make it harder to turn out the low-propensity base voters they need — voters that only Trump has been able to bring to the polls. “These guys are in a pickle,” said one national GOP operative granted anonymity to speak candidly about the landscape, like others in this article. “They may not want Trump to come to the district, but there are still things that Trump can do to help.” Asked what would happen if Trump campaigned in a battleground state where their candidates were running, another GOP operative working on midterm races said: “I suspect my candidates would come down with COVID.” But the candidates may not have much of a choice. Trump is increasingly inserting himself into the election in the closing stretch, ramping up his campaign travel with a slate of stops scheduled in red states, repeatedly imploring voters to “pretend” he’s on the ballot and, most recently, appearing in taxpayer-funded campaign-style ads that the White House has claimed are Public Service Announcements. Some Republicans have encouraged Trump’s team not to send the president to a blue-leaning Omaha district and other key districts where his approval rating is underwater ahead of Election Day, according to two people with direct knowledge of the matter. Brinker Harding is running in the Omaha seat being vacated by retiring Rep. Don Bacon (R-Neb.); his campaign didn’t respond when asked if he’ll attend Trump’s upcoming rally in Grand Island, Nebraska, about a two-hour drive away. Others have said similar things. "They've called me four times now to see if we want him to come, and I've said no," one senior Republican involved in a House GOP battleground race in a district Trump safely won in 2024 told POLITICO. Another Republican operative familiar with Republican midterm strategy said the party views its role — and Trump’s — primarily as driving GOP turnout, while the work of persuading moderates, independents and other swing voters falls more heavily on individual candidates. “Where the president is going is being decided very strategically, to areas where we are trying to boost turnout among Republican voters,” the operative said. “We're not going to be sending him into areas where it would necessarily be hurtful to our candidates.” Others in red states that are increasingly competitive acknowledge that if they want to rally the MAGA base to the degree necessary to hold onto key seats, no one can deliver like Trump. “He's a turnout machine for the Republican Party, the president is,” said Ohio GOP Chair Alex Triantafilou, who will welcome Trump to his state on Saturday. “I certainly know what some of the national polling and some of the pundits have to say about this. But he is always welcome to Ohio because we know that he fires our people up.” Not everyone thinks Trump is a net-positive even in places he comfortably won. A national GOP operative, granted anonymity to speak candidly, said there are “no indications that there are enough turn out voters to overcome dropping some persuasion voters.” Outgoing North Carolina Republican Sen. Thom Tillis said he doesn’t think it would be helpful for Trump to campaign in his state — which the president won in all three of his presidential runs, and where former RNC chair Michael Whatley is struggling to tighten the race against former Gov. Roy Cooper. “Not in my opinion — just if you take a look at the votes — you take a look at the independents. I don't think he's the one who's going to get them out,” he told POLITICO. “I think [Trump’s] job is to get the people out who traditionally vote for him and don't show up in off-year elections,” he added. “Our job [as candidates] is to then … create some separation. It's not like you're breaking your loyalty to the president. ... So there are states I think he should go to, there are states I don't think he should go to." The Whatley campaign, however, feels differently. “Who drives R turnout right now in NC — Trump or Tillis? We would welcome Trump back to NC,” said Whatley’s senior adviser, Jonathan Felts. Both Trump and Vice President JD Vance have been to North Carolina to campaign with Whatley in recent weeks. Trump’s upcoming stop in a red corner of Ohio outside Dayton is part of a broader campaign swing that reflects the political bind. Other stops scheduled include in deep-red states like Oklahoma and Alabama, as well as in red states with key Senate contests including Ohio, Nebraska and Alaska. Ironically, the expanding battleground map could make Trump more useful to Republicans in some of the places they are most worried about. As the fight has spread into states and districts he won by double digits, simply turning out more of his base may be enough to make a difference. The White House argued Trump is the “unequivocal leader, best messenger, and unmatched motivator for the Republican Party.” “No one can dispute the fact that President Trump has created one of the most robust coalitions in political history with the MAGA movement, and the President understands how to communicate with them,” White House spokesperson Davis Ingle said. The Republican National Committee and National Republican Congressional Committee also said Trump is still a valuable turnout tool, and their candidates are eager to have the president visit their districts and to appear with him on the campaign trail. The National Republican Senatorial Committee did not respond to a request for comment. But some of the voters Republicans most need Trump to activate — especially blue-collar white voters in rural areas who came out to vote for him but often skip voting in the midterms — are themselves unhappy with his presidency. Recent POLITICO polling found that even some of Trump’s strongest supporters — those who identify as MAGA — are souring on his handling of key issues. A POLITICO Poll in August found that a 44% plurality of MAGA Trump voters said the Iran war has made things more expensive for them, while 38% said the war has had no real impact on their costs. “It's really Trump's voting base that's feeling the pain of Trump the most,” said another Republican operative involved in several battleground races across the country, granted anonymity to speak candidly about the landscape.“They have to turn those people out. But those people are pissed at Trump, so it's this weird dynamic of like: ‘Does he help? Does he hurt? Can he go and encourage the disenfranchised, the really pissed off Republican Trump voter?’” the operative said. “That's really going to be what decides the outcome of this election.” It’s noteworthy which GOP candidates are enthusiastically coming out to Trump’s rallies — and which are sitting out or staying mum on their plans. A spokesperson confirmed that Sen. Jon Husted (R-Ohio), who is locked in a tough race in a state Trump won by double-digits, will attend Trump’s upcoming rally outside of Dayton; a spokesperson for Vivek Ramaswamy, the GOP gubernatorial candidate, did not respond to an inquiry about Ramaswamy’s attendance plans, nor did spokespeople for the trio of GOP House candidates running in Ohio’s competitive 1st, 7th and 9th Districts. Republican Rep. Ashley Hinson, the GOP Senate candidate in Iowa, recently said the Iran war needs to be “ brought to a successful and immediate end ,” in a rare public break with Trump. Hinson also did not attend a campaign rally Vice President JD Vance held in western Iowa in mid-September . She did, however, appear in the Oval Office behind Trump earlier this week when he announced a plan to build a $15 billion steel plant in Iowa.   But with an ever-darkening environment, some Republicans see any efforts to reverse course as better than nothing. “Everybody sees the polling,” said Daniel Garza, a Texas Republican strategist and president of the conservative LIBRE Initiative . “Is the polling accurate? I have no idea. All I know is that turnout is going to be key to this, and anything helps right now, at this point.” Jordain Carney and Lisa Kashinsky contributed.

stories.headline: Democrats shift away from mail voting amid uncertainty over ballot security and delivery

sources.body: The Supreme Court blocked President Donald Trump’s effort to restrict mail voting. But for Democrats trying to turn out voters, the uncertainty seems harder to put to rest. Fewer Democrats say they plan to vote by mail in November’s midterms than at the same point in 2024, according to a new NBC News poll , as a separate survey finds declining confidence that the Postal Service will deliver election mail on time. That represents an about-face for a party that has increasingly embraced mail voting since the 2020 pandemic election, forcing Democratic strategists to rethink how they get voters to the polls — and how to convince them their ballots will count. Quentin James, founder and president of the Collective PAC, said his group is hearing concerns from Black voters about whether their mailed ballots will be secure and counted. “I think there's confusion,” James said. “We know that the president has spent six months talking about changing the rules regarding mail-in voting, and a lot of folks are concerned about their ballot being secure.” That confusion comes as Democrats and voting groups weigh how to reassure voters after Trump’s latest effort to restrict mail voting. The president signed an executive order in March seeking to crack down on mail-in voting, citing unproven claims that the process is insecure and vulnerable to electoral fraud. “The cheating on mail-in voting is legendary. It’s horrible what’s gone on,” Trump said during an Oval Office signing ceremony. “I think this will help a lot with elections.” Still, the rules for mail ballots — at least nationally — will be effectively the same as 2024 after the Supreme Court rejected the Trump administration’s attempt to enforce the new mail-in ballot delivery regulations in a ruling earlier this month . The high court left in place a lower-court decision that blocked the U.S. Postal Service from implementing the new proposed requirements in the weeks before the midterm election. Despite that, Democratic voters have signaled they are changing how they’ll vote. In the NBC poll, 23% of registered Democrats said they plan to vote by mail, down from 34% in September 2024. Thirty-six percent said they plan to vote early in person, up from 30%, while another 36% expect to vote on Election Day. A Marist poll found that 58% of registered voters were confident the Postal Service would deliver election-related mail to voters and election officials on time, down from 71% in October 2024. Marist also found that Democrats remain more likely than Republicans to plan to vote by mail or absentee ballot, 32% to 12%, respectively. James said his organization has long encouraged early in-person voting through its Rides to Vote program, which provides transportation to voters without a vehicle. But despite the Supreme Court ruling, his organization is also encouraging people considering voting by mail to use a ride voucher to return their completed ballots directly to the required location. “The bigger threat is confusion and fear,” he said. “That is the thing that a court case will not solve, and that's what we're really concerned about.” In Maine, Secretary of State Shenna Bellows said municipal clerks have reported voters canceling absentee ballot requests, including requests to receive ballots automatically in future elections. Bellows cautioned against a blanket message to vote in person. “We would discourage advocates from telling people not to vote by mail if, for those voters, that’s their only option,” said Bellows, a Democrat who ran this cycle for governor and in the rapid-fire Senate primary, pointing to older and disabled Mainers who rely on absentee voting. Her office is instead urging voters to make a plan that works for them, return mailed ballots early and use Maine’s online absentee ballot tracking system to check whether a clerk has received and accepted them. “Our public education efforts have been focused on encouraging voters to make a plan that's right for them, and recognizing that they have the peace of mind of tracking their absentee ballot and the backup option of voting on Election Day if, for any reason, the ballot is delayed by the mail,” Bellows said. Indivisible, one of the party’s largest grassroots groups, is mounting its own early-vote push and nudging people to cast their ballots early, regardless of how they vote. Co-founder Leah Greenberg said that the group is helping organize an Oct. 17 national day of action to encourage people to vote early under their states’ rules. “So we were absolutely hearing concern,” Greenberg said. “But more importantly, what we're hearing is people trying to figure out what they can do and how they can organize locally in order to protect elections.” Greenberg said Indivisible is urging voters to get their ballots in early and emphasizing that a court rejected the administration’s attempt to restrict mail voting. Still, the ruling hasn’t erased the uncertainty organizers say they are hearing from voters. Greenberg and James described a similar mix of relief and concern among voters. “People are glad to hear it, but still wary,” Greenberg said. Democrats, including state election officials who oversee the process, are also looking for ways to boost confidence in the mail system. Nevada Secretary of State Francisco Aguilar has asked his state’s congressional delegation to arrange election observers at postal facilities handling Nevada’s ballots. In letters to the state’s congressional delegation, Aguilar identified sites in Las Vegas and Reno, as well as facilities in West Sacramento, California, and Salt Lake City, Utah. Aguilar said nearly 670,000 Nevadans voted by mail in 2024 and argued that having observers present could strengthen confidence in ballot handling. In an interview, he said observers would also signal to postal workers that they have support in the process. “By having observers there, it gives them the support to say: ‘Hey, we got your back,’” Aguilar said. “We also want to be helpful if there are any concerns — we want to make sure that leadership knows we are not going to stay quiet. We're going to be proactive. We're going to be engaged and we're going to hold them accountable when we need to hold them accountable.” Aguilar said Rep. Susie Lee (D-Nev.) has requested observers following his letters. Lee’s office did not respond to a request for comment. USPS said it had received correspondence regarding Aguilar’s request and was reviewing it. “The Postal Service has successfully delivered America’s election mail, and we are confident that we will do so again this year,” Nikolaj Hagen, a Postal Service spokesperson, said. Hagen pointed to USPS figures showing it delivered 233.3 million pieces of election mail through Aug. 28 in fiscal year 2026, with 97.94% arriving on time. In the 2022 election, USPS handled 105.4 million ballots and delivered 99.93% of those sent by voters to election officials within seven days. In 2024, it handled 222.39 million pieces of ballot mail , with 99.88% delivered to officials within seven days. Meanwhile, Bellows said Maine is taking a different approach. Local USPS representatives have proposed weekly meetings with her election staff, she said, and her office has relationships with workers at the state’s two distribution centers. But she noted congressional observers could be useful in larger states where those relationships are less established. “Maine is a small enough place where, if there were a problem, we would probably know very quickly through union representatives or simply word of mouth,” Bellows said, noting that congressional observers at postal locations could be particularly useful in places “where those relationships may not be as strong or well established.”

sources.body:
La secretaria general de Podemos , Ione Belarra, ha anunciado este jueves que los cuatro diputados de su formación en el Congreso votarán a favor de los dos decretos de vivienda dado que así se lo ha pedido la Confederación de Sindicatos de Inquilinas y que no van a ser la "excusa" para que el Ejecutivo "siga sin hacer nada".

Entrevistada en La Hora de La 1, la diputada que se ha mostrado muy crítica con las medidas aprobadas por el Consejo de Ministros que ha calificado de " migajas ", y ha advertido que "dentro de un mes la gente va a ver que los alquileres siguen por las nubes , que se sigue desahuciando y que el negocio vivienda sigue boyante" porque "hacen negocio con la vida de la gente".

Con la confirmación del apoyo de Podemos a las medidas de vivienda se allana el panorama parlamentario del Gobierno aunque la posición clave para convalidarlas recae en el PNV y Junts , que aún no han apuntado el sentido de su voto de cara a la sesión plenaria en el Congreso de este viernes.

La líder de Podemos ha señalado que más allá del debate parlamentario lo más "interesante" está pasando en las calles, con la movilización por la vivienda, "que la gente se organice, acampe y esté llamando a la huelga general por la vivienda", es "lo mejor" que ha pasado "en muchísimos años".

Además, Belarra ha asegurado que su partido es una "herramienta en manos de los movimientos sociales" y advierte que "se hace mal desoyendo la parte previa que dicen tanto el sindicato de inquilinas como cientos de personas en la calle" que las medidas del Gobierno "son migajas y con migajas no se paga el alquiler", pero "migajas es mejor que nada".

La portavoz de la formación morada en el Congreso ha asegurado que " lo más importante" es que la movilización continúe y ha hecho un llamamiento a participar en la huelga general que pide la acampada de Sol, porque "solo de la movilización van a salir medidas".

sources.body:
Pleno sobre Ceuta en el Congreso de los Diputados Ione Belarra

El tablero parlamentario ha sufrido este jueves su penúltimo movimiento de fichas antes del examen decisivo de mañana en el Congreso. La secretaria general de Podemos, Ione Belarra, ha confirmado que sus cuatro diputados estamparán el sí a los dos reales decretos-ley de vivienda y alquiler aprobados por el Gobierno. Con este paso, la formación morada despeja una de las grandes incógnitas del pleno y traslada el foco -y buena parte de las miradas en la Moncloa- a Junts, que mantiene sus cartas guardadas bajo un manto de “decepción y preocupación”, y, en segundo término, al PNV, que parece inclinarse por aprobar al menos el primero de los decretos.

El viraje de Podemos no se ha producido en el vacío y ha encontrado en el Sindicato de Inquilinos el argumento para explicarlo. Ha sido el colectivo -motor de la marea de protesta que recorre las calles tras el desahucio de Maricarmen- el que ha reclamado expresamente el respaldo parlamentario a los dos decretos. Tras una semana de severas advertencias y amagos de veto, Belarra puede ahora convertir sus reservas iniciales en un voto de apoyo sin necesidad de rebajar un ápice la pirotecnia verbal contra el Ejecutivo.

Poco importa que Belarra haya vuelto a calificar hoy las medidas de “migajas” planteadas por el Ejecutivo ante los micrófonos de TVE o que mantenga su censura a la estrategia de trocear la norma en dos. Lo sustancial es que el partido morado esquiva la fotografía de la discordia -la que le habría alineado en el no junto a las bancadas de PP y Vox- y puede presentar su papeleta como respuesta al “sentir de la calle”, conservando intacta su posición de ariete por la izquierda.

Con el flanco de Podemos encauzado, el foco regresa de forma inequívoca a Junts y al PNV. Y es precisamente el segundo decreto -el relativo a las prórrogas de los contratos y los mecanismos de indemnización- donde el distanciamiento entre Gobierno y sus socios parlamentarios parece más difícil de salvar.

La propia ministra de Vivienda, Isabel Rodríguez, ha tenido que hacer gala este jueves de un pragmatismo casi defensivo. En los micrófonos de la cadena Ser, Rodríguez ha reconocido abiertamente que la arquitectura de apoyos para esta segunda norma “no estaba trabajada como lo está en la otra”, deslizando la posibilidad de una vía alternativa. Si el decreto no logra la convalidación este viernes, el Ejecutivo contempla reactivar su contenido mediante su tramitación como proyecto de ley, ganando así tiempo y margen para la negociación parlamentaria.

La admisión de la ministra revela hasta qué punto los dos decretos llegan mañana al Congreso con una fortaleza parlamentaria desigual. La decisión de dividir el paquete permitió al Gobierno separar las medidas y buscar apoyos diferenciados, pero también ha dejado al descubierto la dificultad de cerrar un acuerdo con Junts sobre el segundo texto.

sources.body:
El aviso rojo de Aemet prevé fuertes lluvias en todo el litoral de Valencia y Castellón 

La Agencia Estatal de Meteorología ha elevado a rojo (peligro extraordinario) a partir de las 18 horas de este jueves el aviso por lluvias en el litoral y en el interior norte de Castellón y en el litoral de Valencia y Tarragona, ante la previsión de que se acumulen 90 litros por metro cuadrado en una hora y hasta 250 litros en doce horas. En su última revisión, Aemet extiende el aviso rojo en esas zonas a mañana viernes, jornada en la que amplía el aviso naranja a la totalidad de la provincia de Alicante.

Aemet espera que a partir de las 18 horas las precipitaciones puedan acumular 90 litros por metro cuadrado en una hora y 250 litros en doce horas en el litoral y el interior norte de la provincia de Castellón, mientras que en el litoral norte de Valencia se podrían acumular 180 litros por metro cuadrado en doce horas.

De esta forma, se eleva un umbral de riesgo que inicialmente se había establecido como naranja (peligro importante) a partir de las 14 horas de este jueves para las provincia de Castellón y Valencia y el litoral norte de Alicante por precipitaciones de 50 l/m2 en una hora y hasta 160 en doce horas. De momento, se Mantiene el aviso naranja en otras áreas de la Comunidad Valenciana, Catalunya y Mallorca.

La Generalitat Valenciana, a través del Centro de Coordinación de Emergencias, ha enviado un es alert a las zonas afectadas de Valencia y Castellón para informar a los habitantes sobre el episodio de fuertes lluvias. El mensaje valenciano se ha recibido también en los móviles de los habitantes de Tarragona más cercanos al territorio de Castellón. “Ante esta situación de peligro extraordinario, deben evitarse desplazamientos y alejarse de ríos y barrancos, así como respetar los cortes de carreteras y, si aumenta el nivel del agua, acceder a las plantas superiores”, recomienda el mensaje.

El conseller de Emergencias e Interior, Juan Carlos Valderrama, preside desde las 11 horas una reunión de coordinación en el Centro de Emergencias de la Generalitat, en L'Eliana (Valencia), a la que asiste la delegada del Gobierno, Pilar Bernabé. Una treintena de municipios de la Comunidad Valenciana suspenderá este jueves las clases a partir de las 13:00 horas y se espera que se sumen más localidades a lo largo de la mañana.

Según la Conselleria de Educación, hasta el momento han informado de la suspensión de las clases una treintena de municipios, entre ellos la ciudad de València, situados en zonas inundables y afectadas por la dana. También se verán afectados la universidad popular, los centros de mayores y los centros ocupacionales.

El Servicio Meteorológico de Catalunya ha actualizado sus previsiones de lluvias intensas previstas para la tarde de hoy, y ha elevado el aviso a peligro muy alto en nueve comarcas, en su mayoría, en la provincia de Tarragona. Las nueve comarcas afectadas por este aviso de peligro muy alto por lluvias torrenciales son Montsià, Baix Ebre, Terra Alta, Baix Camp, Tarragonès, Alt Camp, Alt Penedès, Garraf y Alt Camp. Con esta actualización, Catalunya ha elevado el riesgo a 5 sobre 6 en estas nueve comarcas. La previsión meteorológica es que pueden producirse precipitaciones superiores a los 40 litros por metro cuadrado en 30 minutos hasta las 20 horas de este jueves

sources.body: <p>Cada mañana, nuevos jóvenes aparecen con golpes caminando por las calles de Ceuta: una brecha en la cabeza, un tobillo hinchado, un brazo dislocado, el costado amoratado, una raja de lado a lado de la cara. Y siempre es la misma explicación: me pegaron los soldados. Decenas de testimonios recogidos en distintos puntos de Ceuta entre jóvenes sin relación entre sí, con el único vínculo de dormir cada día a la intemperie en la ciudad autónoma, coinciden al describir las palizas que sufren cada noche a manos del Ejército. Parejas de soldados que irrumpen por la noche entre los cañaverales, las arboledas o las rocas de la playa para aplicar una metodología violenta que comenzó con la llegada masiva de decenas de miles de migrantes hace dos meses. Este martes, Amnistía Internacional recogió <a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-30/amnistia-internacional-denuncia-tortura-y-malos-tratos-a-los-inmigrantes-en-ceuta.html" target="_self" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-09-30/amnistia-internacional-denuncia-tortura-y-malos-tratos-a-los-inmigrantes-en-ceuta.html">en un informe una veintena de casos </a>y los envió a los presidentes del Gobierno español, Pedro Sánchez, y de la ciudad de Ceuta, <a href="https://elpais.com/noticias/juan-jesus-vivas-lara/" rel="" title="https://elpais.com/noticias/juan-jesus-vivas-lara/">Juan Jesús Vivas</a>. Pero los testimonios recogidos por AI no son los únicos. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-01/decenas-de-migrantes-denuncian-agresiones-de-militares-nos-dicen-que-si-no-nos-vamos-seguiran-las-palizas.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>

stories.headline: Spain’s king and queen will visit Ceuta and Melilla in mid-October

sources.body: <p>13 y 14 de octubre. Esos serán los días en los que el rey Felipe VI y Letizia Ortiz visiten Ceuta y Melilla, según han informado este jueves fuentes de la Casa del Rey y de La Moncloa. Viaje al que no les acompañará el presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, según han adelantado desde el Ejecutivo a la agencia Efe y ha confirmado este periódico. Las fechas se habían convertido en el secreto de Estado mejor guardado de los últimos tiempos. Después de dos meses de elucubraciones, expectativas y rifirrafes entre el Gobierno de Ceuta, el Ejecutivo central y Zarzuela, el calendario queda por fin despejado, además, antes de que todos los mandatarios civiles y militares coincidan, con motivo de los fastos de la fiesta nacional, el próximo 12 de octubre. </p><p><a href="https://elpais.com/espana/2026-10-01/los-reyes-visitaran-ceuta-y-melilla-los-dias-13-y-14-de-octubre.html" target="_blank">Seguir leyendo</a></p>
sources.headline: Los Reyes visitarán Ceuta y Melilla los días 13 y 14 de octubre

sources.body:
Dos meses después de desatarse en Ceuta la crisis migratoria los pasados 30 y 31 de julio, en que se produjo la llegada masiva de migrantes irregulares a la ciudad autónoma, se ha confirmado que los reyes Felipe VI y Letizia visitarán Ceuta y Melilla los próximos días 13 y 14 de octubre . Así lo han confirmado fuentes del Ejecutivo y de la Casa Real en dos comunicados idénticos que llegaban prácticamente de forma simultánea.

Según ha podido saber RTVE, el programa de ese viaje, que se ha consensuado entre el Ejecutivo y la Casa del Rey, se dará a conocer en los próximos días. En esa visita Felipe VI no estará acompañado por el presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez . Según fuentes del Ejecutivo podría acompañar a los reyes el ministro de Política Territorial, Ángel Víctor Torres , que ejerce el mando único sobre la situación en Ceuta.

Un día anterior de esa visita a las ciudades autónomas, los reyes habrán presidido en Madrid los actos que conmemoran la Fiesta Nacional, incluido el desfile de las fuerzas armadas.

Esta mañana a su llegada al Congreso, donde ha presidido la inauguración del XII Foro Parlamentario Iberoamericano, los periodistas le han preguntado al rey por esa visita a las ciudades autónomas y, en concreto, si estaba ilusionado. "Como siempre" , se ha limitado a decir el monarca.

“ 🔴 Los reyes visitarán Ceuta y Melilla los próximos 13 y 14 de octubre ▪️ Gobierno y Casa Real han consensuado esta visita, de la que todavía se desconoce agenda 🎙️ @NicoCaballero__ pic.twitter.com/i8BvSQ65V2 “

Este será el primer viaje de Felipe VI a las ciudades autónomas desde su coronación en junio de 2014, y la primera visita de un monarca en los últimos casi 20, desde la que realizó Juan Carlos I en noviembre de 2007.

La cita se producirá dos meses y medio después de que se desatara en Ceuta una grave crisis migratoria, con la llegada masiva de migrantes irregulares, los pasados 30 y 31 de julio. Desde entonces este posible viaje del monarca ha ocupado en varias ocasiones el foco de atención. El pasado 31 de agosto Pedro Sánchez anunció que esa visita se produciría, porque había "razones y argumentos para ello", y señaló que se llevaría a cabo "cuando se den las condiciones".

El anuncio trajo cierta polémica, ya que la oposición acusaba al Ejecutivo de bloquearlo . Indignado, el Gobierno se defendió tachando de " bulo " esa afirmación, que dijeron, expandió la derecha: "No es verdad", dijeron entonces fuentes del Gobierno, "como no es verdad, o no se puede decir que es Rajoy vetara a esa misma visita. Y por eso dijimos que hace 20 años que esto no sucede".

Este jueves se ha anunciado por fin un viaje cuya coordinación se lleva acabo entre Casa Real y el Gobierno de España, ya que según la Constitución el Ejecutivo debe refrendar y autorizar todos los actos públicos y la agenda oficial del monarca. Además, el Gobierno tiene la potestad para dirigir la política exterior de España, por lo que determina cuándo es políticamente oportuno o prudente realizar una visita oficial.

sources.body: L’Ajuntament de Barcelona ha activat en fase d’alerta el Pla d’actuació d’emergència municipal per risc d’insuficiència drenant davant la previsió de les pluges intenses i tempestes previstes per a aquest dijous a la ciutat. Només 24 hores després de desactivar aquest pla pels aiguats que van descarregar a la ciutat dimarts , el consistori torna a demanar prudència a la ciutadania. En aquest sentit, es recomana revisar els desguassos i baixants i desconnectar aparells elèctrics. En el cas dels conductors, es recorda que s’ha de moderar la velocitat i ampliar la distància de seguretat amb la resta de vehicles. També et pot interessar L’Inuncat, en alerta una altra vegada per la previsió de pluja torrencial dijous a Catalunya Manel Cascante Torrella 3 minuts de lectura En alerta també el pla Inuncat Protecció Civil també ha activat en fase d’alerta el pla Inuncat i el Meteocat ha emès avisos d’intensitat de precipitació, amb un llindar màxim de 40 litres en 30 minuts. L‘ avís afecta bona part de Catalunya , inclosos el litoral i prelitoral centrals, durant el matí de dijous (de 8 a 14 h). Es tracta d’un avís de perill de grau alt, 4 sobre una escala de 6, és a dir, indica que hi ha entre un 30 i un 70 % de probabilitat que caiguin més de 40 litres en 30 minuts. El Meteocat ha activat, aquest dijous, l 'avís vermell per pluges torrencials a nou comarques de la meitat sud a la tarda.

El grau de perill màxim de l'avís és del 5 sobre 6 i afectarà les comarques del Montsià, el Baix Ebre, la Terra Alta, el Baix Camp, el Tarragonès, el Baix Penedès, l'Alt Camp, l'Alt Penedès i Garraf.

Protecció Civil ha enviat aquest migdia un missatge Es-Alert a la població del Baix Camp, el Tarragonès, el Baix Penedès, l'Alt Camp, l'Alt Penedès i Garraf demanant que s' extremin les precaucions en la mobilitat i evitin acostar-se a zones inundables . També recordaran que en cas d'emergència truquin al 112.

Una mica més tard, han enviat un altre missatge a la població del Montsià, el Baix Ebre i la Terra Alta, on s'espera que les pluges triguin una mica més en arribar.

Sobre la una de la tarda, Protecció Civil ha publicat a les xarxes socials un avís de temps violent durant les properes dues hores per risc de pedra, ratxes de vent, esclafits o tornados al Tarragonès, Alt i Baix Camp, Aly i Baix Penedès i Garraf.

La pluja està previst que comenci cap al migdia a les comarques del Penedès i Garraf i que vagin cap al sud, on a la zona de l'Ebre es pot fer especialment intensa ja al vespre, nit i matinada. A partir de demà les pluges es concentraran especialment a la zona de l'Ebre i el temporal pot allargar-se fins el dissabte al vespre.

El Meteocat manté l' alerta taronja a les comarques del Priorat i la Ribera d'Ebre, la Conca de Barberà, l'Anoia, el Baix Llobregat, la Noguera, la Segarra, el Bages, el Solsonès, el Beguedà, el Moianès, el Lluçanès i Osona .

Aquest episodi de pluges arriba tres dies després les precipitacions torrencials aquest dimarts a l'àrea de Barcelona, de Girona i a l'Alt Penedès .

Protecció Civil manté activada l' alerta del pla Inuncat davant la previsió de pluja intensa a bona part del país. Aquest dijous la subdirectora de Protecció Civil, Imma Soler , ha insistit en la "precaució i la previsió" per evitar incidents durant l'episodi de pluges i ha insistit en la importància d'allunyar-se de rius, rieres i zones inundables.

També ha demanat a la població que hagi agafar el cotxe o altres vehicles que prioritzin les vies principals i evitin les secundaries i que no aparquin en zones inundables. També ha demanat que no vagin a buscar el vehicle si l'han deixat en algun pàrquing que pugui quedar afectat per l'aigua.

Protecció Civil enviarà un primer ES-Alert al Garraf, l'Alt Penedès, el Baix Penedès, l'Alt Camp, el Tarragonès i el Baix Camp per pluges intenses des del migdia i durant la tarda i un segon al Montsià, Baix Ebre i Terra Alta a partir del vespre https://t.co/hE3n8qR89s pic.twitter.com/gOrWHJsXj5

Per la seva banda, el cap de predicció del Meteocat, Santi Segalà , ha recordat que les tempestes poden afectar qualsevol punt del territori. Preocupa especialment, però, la zona de les Terres de l'Ebre on la pluja serà molt intensa i es pot mantenir durant més de 12 hores .

Santi Segalà, cap de l'Àrea de Predicció del Servei Meteorològic de Catalunya, adverteix que a les Terres de l'Ebre l'episodi "pot deixar 200 litres per metre quadrat" https://t.co/hE3n8qR89s pic.twitter.com/M9Hw6rkv31

Protecció Civil ha enviado una alerta a los móviles de Tarragona, el Penedès y el Garraf por el episodio de lluvias este jueves. / Miquel Codolar

Protecció Civil ha enviado una alerta a los móviles para pedir que se extremen las precauciones ante la previsión de lluvias en el Penedès y el Camp de Tarragona . Lo ha hecho poco antes de las 13:00 horas de este jueves, en el inicio del episodio de fuertes precipitaciones que se prevén en el sur de Catalunya a lo largo del día.

El primer aviso de Protecció Civil este jueves, que ha servido para alertar de las lluvias intensas del mediodía y durante la tarde. Las comarcas alertadas, de momento, han sido Garraf, Alt Penedès, Baix Penedès, Alt Camp, Baix Camp y Tarragonès .

Durante las próximas dos horas existe riesgo de granizo, rachas fuertes de viento, reventones o tornados en estas comarcas. Ante esta situación, se recomienda extremar las precauciones.

Se trata del segundo ES-Alert que se envía a las comarcas litorales de Tarragona y el Penedès esta semana, tras el recibido el pasado lunes 28 de septiembre por la noche.

La Agencia Estatal de Meteorología (AEMET) también ha activado un aviso rojo por lluvias intensas en el litoral de Tarragona y en el interior norte y litoral de Castelló, que se mantendrá durante la tarde y la primera mitad del viernes. Ante esta situación, la Confederación Hidrográfica del Ebro (CHE) ha intensificado la vigilancia en el río y advierte de que las precipitaciones pueden provocar crecidas súbitas en barrancos, cauces menores y otros puntos donde se registren lluvias de especial intensidad.

Habrá un segundo mensaje ES-Alert a la Terra Alta, el Baix Ebre y el Montsià , donde la previsión es para la tarde y la noche.

La atención, según apuntan, estará especialmente centrada en las Terres de l'Ebre, donde se puede superar el umbral de 90 l/m² en tres horas varias veces y acumular más de 200 litros en el total del episodio. Además, en esta zona el temporal de lluvias podría quedar estacionado y durar hasta 18 horas.

stories.headline: Catalan government says it will not clear Barcelona’s housing-rights encampment

sources.body: (ACN/Redacció) La consellera d’Interior, Núria Parlon , ha assegurat que no tenen previst aixecar l ‘ acampada de la plaça de Catalunya pel dret a l’habitatge . “El que ens toca és ser respectuosos amb aquesta mobilització “, ha dit a RAC1. La consellera ha considerat que “socialment no s’entendria” que el Departament d’Interior o la Guàrdia Urbana de Barcelona “no respectessin aquest dret de protesta” davant d’un problema que, ha dit, afecta molta gent. També ha dit que l’exercici d’aquest dret a protesta ha de ser “respectuós” amb altres drets i dins d’unes “mínimes regles de conducta”. També et pot interessar El Sindicat de Llogateres se suma a l’acampada pel dret a l’habitatge de la plaça de Catalunya Marta Casals Torres 2 minuts de lectura La consellera ha dit que és “esperable” que la protesta duri mentre es mantingui la pressió per l’aprovació dels decrets del Govern espanyol en matèria d’habitatge. En aquest sentit, ha dit que tant l’executiu de Pedro Sánchez com el català ja estan posant en marxa iniciatives en aquest àmbit. El Sindicat de Llogateres se suma a l’acampada Aquest dijous el Sindicat de Llogateres s’ha sumat a l’acampada pel dret a l’habitatge i ha animat la ciutadania a unir-s’hi. El portaveu de l’entitat, Enric Aragonès, també ha recordat que hi haurà una cassolada aquest dijous a les 20 h a les places dels ajuntaments i que, a Barcelona, es farà a la plaça de Sant Jaume i, a més, que dissabte també hi ha convocada una manifestació a l’Hospitalet de Llobregat. També et pot interessar Gairebé la meitat de les persones de 30 a 44 anys són llogateres, 20 punts més que fa una dècada Redacció 2 minuts de lectura

sources.body:
Creix l'acampada a la plaça Catalunya de Barcelona per reclamar millores socials entorn a l'habitatge , després d'una primera nit de protesta. Aquest dimecres, hi han arribat més persones per donar-hi suport i s'hi han instal·lat més tendes de campanya.

Els concentrats expliquen que han passat una primera nit tranquil·la i que tenen previst quedar-s'hi fins divendres , tot i que no descarten allargar.

Aquest dimecres a la tarda, han tallat la ronda de Sant Pere durant quinze minuts, amb una pancarta on s'hi llegia "No permetrem cap desnonament més".

La reivindicació coincideix amb l'aprovació aquest dimarts al Consell de Ministres de dos decrets en matèria d'habitatge i arriba quatre dies després de l'acampada a la Puerta del Sol , a Madrid, arran del desnonament de la Maricarmen .

Volen lluitar, també, contra el sensellarisme. Una de les que hi ha passat la nit, Elena Martí , ho ha explicat: "Va per tota la gent que està vivint al carrer, que ja ha estat desnonada, que no té accés a l'habitatge, que està vivint amb pensions o a cases de familiars".

Un dels altres concentrats, Arteko , ha parlat de les tendes de campanya que es veuen a la Zona Franca o a Montjuïc: "No són pas reivindicacions polítiques; són acampades de gent vulnerable i molt precaritzada".

La concentració aplega persones a títol individual, així com membres de diferents moviments i assembles:

Una publicación compartida por 3CatInfo (@3catinfo)

L'embrió de l'acampada es va gestar aquest dilluns , després de la concentració de protesta davant del Palau de Congressos de Barcelona aprofitant la presència al recinte del president del govern espanyol, Pedro Sánchez.

Després d'aquesta acció, una trentena de persones es van reunir a la plaça Catalunya i van fer una assemblea ja amb la intenció de fer acampada. Finalment, la reivindicació s'ha materialitzat aquest dimarts.

De moment, el Sindicat de Llogateres no ha fet cap crida a participar-hi.

El seu portaveu, Enric Aragonès , en una entrevista a 3CatInfo, ha valorat l'aprovació dels decrets per part de Consell de Ministres:

Cal anar molt més enllà, abaixar el preu del lloguer, acabar amb l'especulació, ampliar el parc d'habitatge públic. Hem de canviar les regles del joc.

El Sindicat de Llogateres, el Sindicat d'Habitatge Socialista de Catalunya (SHSC) i altres entitats han convocat una manifestació aquest dissabte a l'Hospitalet de Llobregat per continuar pressionant el govern espanyol i els seus socis per tirar endavant els dos decrets al Congrés.

Fonts del SHSC han explicat que la protesta va ser convocada inicialment pel suïcidi d'una dona després de ser desnonada del seu habitatge a l'Hospitalet.
sources.headline: L'acampada per l'habitatge de Barcelona creix i diuen que s'hi quedaran almenys fins divendres

sources.body:
La plaça de Catalunya es llevava aquest dimecres amb una escena que no es veia des de feia quinze anys . Com ja es va fer el 2011 sota el moviment del 15-M , prop de 150 persones van tornar a plantar tendes de campanya dimarts al vespre al bell mig d’aquest punt cèntric de la capital catalana per demanar mesures reals que garanteixin el dret a l’habitatge . Ho van fer de manera pràcticament espontània, sense seguir les directrius de cap sindicat o agrupació, i com a resposta a la gran mobilització que dilluns va tallar l’avinguda Diagonal durant prop de quatre hores. “ Feia dies que a Madrid ja estaven acampats i anàvem tard . Barcelona no es podia quedar enrere “, explica l’Arteko, activista veterà del Sindicat d’Habitatge del Raval i un dels portaveus del col·lectiu. L’èxit de la convocatòria va sorprendre els mateixos implicats i aquest migdia encara estaven provant d’organitzar els inquilins de les prop d’un centenar de tendes que omplen la part central de la plaça.

Una de les persones que va acudir aquest dimarts al vespre a la crida va ser la Sofia. Aquesta jove de 25 anys va participar de la concentració de dilluns, on va conèixer molts dels companys amb qui ha passat aquesta primera nit al ras. “Anava preguntant a tothom si aquí es faria o no… Tot això em toca de ple i crec que acampar és l’única manera real de fer pressió, incomodar i donar visibilitat al problema “, assenyala, tot traient el cap des de la tenda que comparteix amb dues persones més. Considera que els dos decrets que el govern espanyol portarà al Congrés dels Diputats divendres són “ paper mullat ” i només un “ pegat ” que no va a l’arrel del problema. Per tot això, té clar que l’acampada continuarà independentment de l’aprovació o no de les mesures . “Haurem d’esperar a tenir el text concret per decidir, però ja sabem que el que s’aprovi no serà prou”, lamenta.

A l’altra banda del campament, tres joves conversaven aquest dimecres al migdia mentre observaven la forta expectació mediàtica despertada per l’acampada. “ Vam decidir sumar-nos perquè no podem independitzar-nos i l’habitatge és, cada cop més, un negoci “, deia la Marta. “Una habitació als barris de Sant Roc (Badalona) o la Mina (Sant Adrià de Besòs) ja et costa més de 330 euros “, incidia en Jonathan. “També volem reivindicar que el problema és l’especulació i no la immigració”, afegia la Marina. Els tres amics creuen que Barcelona fa dies que hauria d’haver seguit l’exemple de la Puerta del Sol de Madrid i subratllen que l’accés a l’habitatge és un problema que afecta la majoria de la població. “ Molts vivim amb els pares o treballem només per poder pagar el lloguer d’una habitació perquè el d’un pis és impossible “, reblaven. Sobre l’aprovació dels decrets i una possible dissolució del campament, els joves ho tenen clar: “Són mesures dissuasives i, la més ambiciosa (la dels contractes indefinits), ni tan sols tirarà endavant […] De moment, l’acampada és indefinida “.
